title: Exercise Tarang Shakti: A Mirror to India’s Multipronged Engagements
author: Dinakar Peri
text:
An Indian Air Force HAL Tejas leads a formation of a Mikoyan MiG-29UPG, Dassault Mirage 2000, Dassault Rafale, SEPECAT Jaguar, and Sukhoi Su-30MKI during Tarang Shakti 26 over Jodhpur, India, Oct. 2, 2026.
Credit: U.S. Air Force photo by Airman 1st Class Nathaniel Jackson
“The defense relationships of the future will be about technology and trust, not just about platforms,” India’s Defense Minister Rajnath Singh said at an event and demonstration in Jodhpur on October 10 as the multilateral Exercise Tarang Shakti neared its end. A fly-past after that featured an arrow-shaped formation that included the Indian Air Force Su-30MKI (Russian origin) at the center, flanked on one side by a U.S. F-35 and an Indian Light Combat Aircraft (LCA), and on the other side by a French Rafale and an F-16 of the United Arab Emirates Air Force. This was an impressive formation; the technology and firepower they represented cannot be easily beaten.An American fifth-generation fighter flying alongside a Russian-origin jet bears testimony to India’s multi-pronged foreign policy and military engagements.[...]
